title: Machine Learning
tagline: Classic ML the way practitioners use it: regression, trees, boosting, evaluation, and scikit-learn.

steps.title: Bias and variance
steps.why: The trade-off behind every modeling decision.

steps.title: Linear regression
steps.why: The simplest model, and the one everything else gets compared to.

steps.title: Gradient descent
steps.why: How models actually learn, step by step.

steps.title: Logistic regression
steps.why: Your first classifier, and still a strong baseline.

steps.title: Cross-validation
steps.why: How to know if your model works on data it hasn't seen.

steps.title: The confusion matrix
steps.why: Accuracy lies. Precision and recall don't.

steps.title: ROC and AUC
steps.why: Compare classifiers across every threshold at once.

steps.title: Decision trees
steps.why: Readable models that split data into simple rules.

steps.title: Random forests
steps.why: Many trees beat one tree. Still a top choice for tabular data.

steps.title: Gradient boosting
steps.why: The idea behind the models that win Kaggle tabular competitions.

steps.title: XGBoost
steps.why: The library that made boosting fast and famous.

steps.title: K-means clustering
steps.why: Find groups in data with no labels.

steps.title: PCA
steps.why: Squash many features into a few you can actually look at.

steps.title: Scikit-learn in practice
steps.why: Put it all together with the library everyone uses.

projects: Enter Kaggle's Titanic or House Prices competition with a cross-validated scikit-learn pipeline.
On an imbalanced dataset, plot precision and recall as you move the threshold, and pick one for a stated cost.
Compare logistic regression, a random forest, and XGBoost on the same splits and explain the gap.
